subject: Improper flat prior for strictly positive parameter?

messages.author: 46f76d1903dc6874
messages.subject: Improper flat prior for strictly positive parameter?
parts:
Hi All,

Is there a workaround to use an improper flat prior for a variance term? I tried using T() with dflat() but learned shorty thereafter that T() doesn't work with dflat(). Any help would be much appreciated!

Thanks!
Vincent

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Improper flat prior for strictly positive parameter?
parts:
Another option provided in NIMBLE is the dhalfflat() distribution, which is an improper prior with positive support: (0, +Inf), e.g.:

variance_term ~ dhalfflat()

This might be just what you're looking for.
On Fri, Dec 6, 2019 at 1:08 AM Perry de Valpine <pdeva...@berkeley.edu> wrote:

How about dunif(0, 1000), or whatever big number you need for the upper limit?

Thanks!
